items.title: Meta fined €805m for accessing users’ photos, videos without consent
items.description: Italian regulators fined Facebook parent company Meta 805 million euros ($880 million) for accessing users’ photos without their “specific” consent, the country’s data protection authority said on Saturday. Through the Facebook application for Android devices, Meta accessed photographs, videos and related metadata belonging to Italian users “without obtaining specific consent and without properly informing them”, the authority said in a statement. Meta said it would appeal the decision. A company spokesperson said “we strongly disagree” with the assessment by the regulators “and the disproportionate level of the fine”. In late October, authorities in New Mexico ordered Meta to pay $25 billion for having misled the state’s residents for more than a decade over use of their data — a record fine for the company, which slammed it as a “tax” on freedom of expression. Saturday’s latest fine is among the largest an Italian authority has ever imposed on a tech giant. In 2021, Amazon received a more than 1.1-billion-euro fine for breaching competition law. That sum was subsequently reduced to 752 million euros on appeal. – Facebook gallery feature – The Italian penalty imposed on Facebook relates to its gallery suggestions feature, available since 2023, which suggests photos and videos from a user’s phone gallery as ideas for posts as they are browsing. According to Italy’s regulator, Facebook requested access to the gallery via a single authorisation valid for the entire app, preceded by a generic notice requesting enabling of other features, which did not allow users to understand that they were also authorising suggestions from their gallery. The regulator said Meta would now have to seek consent by means of a separate and specific request for the feature concerned and clearly signpost what it is used for, namely that it involves access to a user’s photo gallery, as well as how to disable it. In determining the size of the fine, the authority said it took into account “the high number of people affected” — around 20 million Android users in Italy — and the duration of the infringement, “which is still ongoing for those who have not updated the app and for those who have already given their consent to the system”. The authority also cited “Meta’s lack of cooperation during the investigation”. It imposed a fine amounting to roughly 0.4 per cent of the group’s annual turnover, which hit $201 billion in 2025, for a net profit of $60.5 billion. The post Meta fined €805m for accessing users’ photos, videos without consent appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Hold APC responsible if anything happens to Nigeria’s democracy — Wabara
items.description: . Rejects Appeal Court ruling on PDP leadership crisis . Warns against making Tinubu sole presidential candidate By Steve Oko UMUAHIA – Former Senate President and Chairman of the Board of Trustees (BoT) of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Senator Adolphus Wabara, has warned the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to accept responsibility should Nigerias democracy suffer any setback arising from what he described as the systematic weakening of opposition parties. Wabara, who expressed strong reservations over the recent Court of Appeal judgment in the PDP leadership dispute, accused the ruling party of benefiting from the protracted crises in opposition parties and warned that attempts to weaken political alternatives ahead of the 2027 general elections could undermine Nigeria’s democratic foundations. He described the appellate court’s refusal to compel the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to recognise his faction’s position as a travesty of justice, insisting that the circumstances surrounding the emergence of the Alhaji Abdulrahman Muhammad-led faction raised serious questions about democracy in Nigeria. The former Senate President warned that accepting the Muhammad-led faction’s position without adequately addressing the issues surrounding its emergence amounted to “standing truth in the head”. The Court of Appeal, in a unanimous decision by a three-member panel, had declined to disturb the July 17, 2026 judgment of the Federal High Court in Abuja, which dismissed the suit filed by the Wabara-led BoT faction. The appellate court held that the trial judge, Justice Salim Ibrahim, was right to dismiss the suit seeking to validate actions taken on behalf of the PDP by the Tanimu Turaki, SAN-led faction. Those actions included a national convention organised by the faction, which subsequently announced former President Goodluck Jonathan as its consensus presidential candidate for the 2027 election. In the lead judgment delivered virtually by Justice R. O. Ayoola, the appellate court held that the Wabara-led group lacked the locus standi to institute the action on behalf of the PDP. It consequently struck out the party’s name as the eighth appellant and held that the appeal had become academic and amounted to an abuse of judicial process. Reacting to the judgment, Wabara expressed bewilderment at what he described as its questionable legal reasoning, wondering how the appellate court arrived at what he called an inverted interpretation of the issues before it. He cautioned the judiciary against becoming entangled in political disputes in ways that could further erode public confidence in the institution. According to him, the growing legal battles within opposition parties, particularly the PDP, the African Democratic Congress (ADC), and the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, have raised troubling questions about the ability of opposition parties to participate effectively in the 2027 elections. Wabara alleged that the APC was benefiting from the weakening of opposition parties and urged the judiciary to protect its independence and credibility by ensuring that its decisions do not create the impression of favouring any political interest. “The opposition should be allowed to breathe. Nigeria cannot afford a situation where formidable opposition parties are weakened to the point that nobody can effectively challenge the ruling party in 2027. “Tinubu should not be made a sole presidential candidate in 2027. That would be anti-democratic and a dangerous precedent capable of bringing avoidable embarrassment to our country. “Using the courts to make Tinubu the sole presidential candidate in 2027 will not save the APC,” he declared. The PDP chieftain, who recalled that the APC itself benefited from a competitive political environment before taking power in 2015, challenged the ruling party to demonstrate its confidence in its performance by allowing opposition parties to operate freely. “Would the APC have been in power today if the PDP had used the courts to cripple opposition parties when it was in government? Democracy thrives on competition, not the elimination of competitors,” Wabara said.. The former Senate President also expressed concern over the recent court ruling in the leadership crisis rocking the ADC, warning that developments in the three major opposition parties could leave Nigeria with a significantly weakened opposition ahead of the next general elections. “From the look of things, no opposition party is yet free from the ongoing political persecution and grand plot to weaken the opposition ahead of 2027,” he alleged. He said he was increasingly doubtful whether the opposition parties would be allowed to provide credible alternatives to the APC in the forthcoming elections. Wabara also condemned reported incidents of political violence and attacks against opposition members in different parts of the country, challenging the authorities to investigate the incidents and bring perpetrators to justice. He said the government should demonstrate, through concrete action, that it was committed to protecting the rights of all political parties to campaign, mobilise and canvass for votes without intimidation. Wabara stressed that Nigeria’s peace, unity and democratic stability must take precedence over the political ambitions of any individual or party. “The peace and unity of Nigeria are bigger than the ambition of any individual or political party. Nobody should be allowed to toy with our democracy,” he warned. He, however, expressed confidence that the APC would face a difficult electoral contest in 2027, insisting that Nigerians would not reward a government “they believe has subjected them to hardship and economic retrogression.” “Nigerians will not be renewing hardship and retrogression in 2027,” he declared. Wabara called on opposition parties to close ranks, overcome their internal differences and consider presenting a consensus presidential candidate capable of mounting a formidable challenge to the ruling party. He described opposition unity as the ruling party’s biggest nightmare, urging opposition leaders to place the country’s democratic future above personal ambitions. He also appealed to Nigerians to vote according to their convictions and resist financial inducements or other forms of pressure designed to compromise their electoral choices. The former Senate President called on the international community to move beyond routine election observation and speak out against developments capable of weakening democratic institutions and political competition in Nigeria. “Separating a squabble is better than calling for a ceasefire in the middle of a war,” Wabara said, urging stakeholders to address the underlying political tensions before they escalate into a wider democratic crisis. items.title: La Tunisie connaît une nette relance du tourisme de croisière
items.description: Les ports tunisiens ont accueilli 165 navires de croisière entre janvier et octobre 2026, contre 127 navires sur l’ensemble de l’année 2025, a indiqué le ministre du Tourisme et de l’Artisanat, Sofiene Tekaya, soulignant une reprise du tourisme de croisière durement affecté après l’attaque terroriste du musée du Bardo le 18 mars 2015, qui a coûté la vie à 21 touristes qui venaient de débarquer d’un bateau de croisière accosté au port de La Goulette. Répondant aux interventions des membres de l’Assemblée des représentants du peuple (ARP) et du Conseil national des régions et des districts (CNRD), ce dimanche 15 novembre 2026 — dans le cadre d’une séance plénière conjointe consacrée à l’examen du budget du ministère pour l’exercice 2027 —, le ministre a expliqué que ces escales ont contribué à dynamiser l’activité économique, notamment grâce à l’organisation d’excursions vers des sites historiques, naturels et des monuments, ainsi que vers les marchés d’artisanat. Il a ajouté que son ministère œuvre à étendre les activités de croisière aux ports de Sousse et de Zarzis, qui connaît actuellement des travaux d’aménagement afin d’attirer davantage de navires. M. Tekaya a également souligné les efforts déployés pour relier ces escales aux villages artisanaux, aux sites archéologiques et culturels, ainsi qu’à d’autres zones touristiques — en particulier dans le sud de la Tunisie —, dans le but de permettre aux différentes régions de mieux tirer profit de cette activité touristique. Rappelons l’évolution du tourisme de croisière en Tunisie entre 2010 et 2026 se caractérise par une phase d’âge d’or avant la révolution, un effondrement prolongé dû aux crises sécuritaires et politiques, puis une reprise progressive et affirmée ces dernières années. 2010 est considérée comme l’année de référence historique pour cette activité en Tunisie, qui avait alors accueilli environ 1 million de croisiéristes, principalement via le port de La Goulette, au nord de Tunis, jadis escale incontournable des grands paquebots en Méditerranée. Après la révolution de 2011 et les attentats terroristes ayant directement visé le secteur du tourisme et des excursions (Sousse, Bardo), les grands croisiéristes internationaux (Costa, MSC…) se sont désengagés de la Tunisie et le secteur a connu un véritable effondrement, avant de reprendre timidement au lendemain de la crise de la Covid-19, en 2021. I. B. L’article La Tunisie connaît une nette relance du tourisme de croisière est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Talent without principles can lead you astray, Rwandan author warns
items.description: Rwandan author, Lisa Munezero, has warned that people with talent but no principles can go astray, saying fulfilling one’s purpose requires integrity and uprightness. Munezero also said Rwanda’s post-genocide generation needs healing, adding that her book, titled: ‘The Well of Knowing’, seeks to contribute to that process. The business expert spoke at the book’s launch in Lagos, where she said the publication seeks to change how the world sees Africa. She said: “Whatever you are good at, any talent you have, but if you don’t have principles in your life, if you don’t know how to set boundaries, if you don’t know what you should do, what you have to avoid, you always find yourself in a place where you shouldn’t be. Everyone should know their purpose. Even for Christians, the Bible says, it’s not something people created. It’s something that even God created us to fill. There is a space we have to fill in this life. Purpose tells you why.” On how she started writing, she said: “My journey to write started when I was a little girl. When it started, I can say it was in a form of healing. In Rwanda in 1994, there was a genocide against the Tutsi. I was born after the genocide. I grew up in a society where it started from zero. Families, government, everyone. As far as I remember, when I was in primary school, I used to write. I liked to write. In 2017, I wanted to write a book. “I used to write some stories. Different things related to content of healing, reconciliation, like other students. I had the privilege to write about how people like me, young generation, who were born after the genocide, came here. We needed to heal too. We grew up in a family that lost so many people. Others were in jail. Some students used to say that fathers of family members are dead because of what they did. They feel ashamed. It was a challenge to me. After that, because I used to love to write, I found out that I’m a good writer because when I used to write, to teach, people used to come to me and say, I feel my life has changed. “Wherever I am, I want to show that I’m from Africa. I want people to respect Africa as much as they respect other people from other continents. I chose to write something that I live in my life. My experience, my background, and African stories. In this book, there is testimony of Africa. I chose to go that way.” Also speaking at the event, one of the book’s reviewers, Adekunle Adekenambi, said that, unlike many other books, ‘The Well of Knowing’ contains several examples drawn from African experiences. According to him, everyone interested in living a successful life, running a successful business or leading a successful family or administration should read the book. He said: “As a father, I picked something from the book. Do not force your child to do anything. Rather, study the child, what are his abilities, and try as much as possible to encourage it and build it. The writer used everyday language and the explanation of concepts is very simple and highly understandable. The writer explains concepts like purposes, principles, in such a way that an ordinary reader will understand them in such different ways from what we used to know.” Another book reviewer, Anote Ajeluorou, said in the first part of the book, Munezero focuses on the qualities aspiring entrepreneurs should possess. He added that she identifies six pairs of qualities: purpose and direction, potential and principles, power and knowledge, wisdom and discipline, strength and well-being, and rejection and dissonance. He said: “As can be seen, Munezero has not necessarily invented new ideas or business concepts. These are familiar ways and concepts that we throw around every day. They are probably not the standard classroom concepts, but the sheer practicality of the application to every business life is what makes this book an interior one. Let’s remember that Munezero started out as a child who was curious about market women running their businesses. She paid close attention to these women, how they conducted their businesses, their customer care approaches, their sales pitches, and how they organised their businesses. “She was quick enough to want to venture into sales as she grew older. Then her father recognised this early interest. Instead of only encouraging it, he invested in it even though he wanted a different kind of path in their sales for her daughter. “As with most parents, he wanted to project his own career ambition on her daughter. But he also recognised her daughter’s early curiosity and bought her a business book which would later potentially give birth to this, but even if not directly.” Meanwhile, Donatus Chimaobi of Whitefield High School said the book’s discussion of discovering one’s purpose encouraged him to reflect on what mattered most to him. He said: “In discovering purpose, you must ask yourself what is important to you. I really loved that sentence. What is important to you? It really made me sit and think because, I want to be a lawyer, I want to study law, I want to study law, I want to study law. When that phrase hit me, I was like, what is important to me? When I say I want to be a lawyer, what is important to me? And it made me think that I really hate injustice.” The post Talent without principles can lead you astray, Rwandan author warns appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Gala des Étoiles : et si nos racines étaient notre meilleur tapis rouge ? ( par Arame NDIAYE)
items.description: La deuxième édition du Gala des Étoiles a fait parler d’elle sur les réseaux sociaux, notamment sur TikTok. Des tenues extravagantes, des inspirations animales et une bonne dose de créativité. De quoi rappeler, à une autre échelle, le célèbre Met Gala. Mais au-delà du spectacle, une question mérite d’être posée : et si nous osions davantage puiser dans notre patrimoine culturel pour habiller nos grands rendez-vous ? Le Sénégal aussi a son petit Met Gala ! Enfin, façon de parler. Depuis la deuxième édition du Gala des Étoiles, les réseaux sociaux ont trouvé de quoi alimenter leurs discussions. Sur TikTok particulièrement, les tenues des célébrités ont suscité commentaires, comparaisons, moqueries parfois, mais aussi admiration. Chacun y est allé de son analyse, de son classement et de son petit verdict sur les looks de la soirée. Il faut dire que le spectacle était au rendez-vous. Le thème de la nature a inspiré des créations aussi audacieuses que surprenantes. Scorpion, lion, paon, serpent… La faune s'est invitée sur le tapis rouge, avec des personnalités qui ont joué le jeu jusqu'au bout. On aurait presque cru assister à une parade dans une jungle version haute couture ! Impossible, dès lors, de ne pas penser au Met Gala, ce rendez-vous new-yorkais où les célébrités rivalisent d'imagination pour interpréter un thème à travers des tenues parfois improbables. Bien sûr, les deux événements n'ont ni la même envergure ni les mêmes moyens. Mais ils partagent cette volonté de faire de la mode un spectacle et du vêtement un moyen d'expression. Seulement voilà, dans cette course à l'originalité, une piste mérite peut-être davantage d'attention : nos racines. Car si la nature peut inspirer les créateurs, notre patrimoine culturel regorge lui aussi de trésors capables de nourrir les imaginaires. Pourquoi ne pas aller chercher dans nos étoffes traditionnelles, nos bijoux, nos coiffures, nos parures, nos symboles et nos savoir-faire artisanaux ? Le Sénégal n'a pourtant pas besoin d'aller très loin pour trouver de quoi faire sensation. Du thioub aux broderies du Fouta, du pagne tissé aux bijoux traditionnels, des parures léboues aux tenues d'apparat sérères, il existe une richesse vestimentaire qui pourrait donner naissance à des créations spectaculaires. Il ne s'agit pas de ressortir les tenues d'antan telles quelles, mais de les réinterpréter avec une touche contemporaine. De faire dialoguer héritage et modernité, sans transformer nos traditions en simples accessoires de décoration. La cérémonie d'ouverture des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026 en a d'ailleurs donné un aperçu intéressant. En faisant une place aux références culturelles africaines et sénégalaises dans sa mise en scène, elle a montré que nos imaginaires peuvent aussi nourrir de grandes productions visuelles. Nos identités, nos couleurs et nos traditions ont de quoi émerveiller lorsqu'elles sont mises en valeur avec audace et créativité. Le Gala des Étoiles pourrait ainsi devenir davantage qu'un rendez-vous où l'on scrute les tenues des célébrités. Il pourrait être une vitrine pour les stylistes locaux, un espace d'expérimentation et surtout une occasion de raconter le Sénégal à travers ses vêtements. Car l'originalité ne consiste pas forcément à ressembler à ce qui se fait ailleurs, ni à rivaliser avec les grandes scènes internationales. Arame NDIAYE

items.title: Saudi Masam project clears 1,289 mines in Yemen
items.description: RIYADH: Members of Saudi Arabia’s Masam project removed 1,289 explosive devices from various regions of Yemen last week. items.title: Two dead as car fleeing police crashes in UK
items.description: By Juliet Umeh Two people have died after a car being pursued by police collided with their vehicle in Leeds, a city in West Yorkshire in northern England, UK. According to a report, West Yorkshire Police said a blue BMW 123D “failed to stop” for a police vehicle on Gelderd Road at 12:44 a.m. on Sunday. Officers began a pursuit, during which the BMW collided with a white Volkswagen Scirocco turning into Gelderd Road from Lowfields Road. The media report said that the driver of the Volkswagen, a 22-year-old man from York, died at the scene. It said: “His passenger, a 23-year-old woman, also from York, died in hospital a short time later. “A 39-year-old man from Harrogate, who was in the BMW, was arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving and driving while over the prescribed limit for cannabis. He remains in custody. “Three other occupants of the BMW – two boys aged 16 and 17, and a 16-year-old girl – were taken to hospital with injuries police said were not life-threatening. They have also been arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving. “The Independent Office for Police Conduct has declared an independent investigation after a referral from West Yorkshire Police. “Gelderd Road remained closed, with drivers advised to avoid the area and use alternative routes,” the report added. The post Two dead as car fleeing police crashes in UK appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Charme francophone (le billet de Omar DIOUF)
items.description: « Bonne voyage ! » Depuis tout jeune, nous entendions cette expression dite dans la plus grande gentillesse pour souhaiter une route paisible à un parent ou un ami embarqué dans un véhicule. C’était en Casamance et avec le temps, en grandissant, nous remarquons que ce vœu est toujours répété avec le plus grand sérieux du monde par certaines vieilles personnes. À quoi bon les rectifier, si nous savons qu’en Afrique, la langue de Molière est souvent parlée comme l’on « mangerait de la bonne confiture ». Un charme qui amène l’Académie française à inclure plusieurs mots et expressions d’origine africaine dans le dictionnaire. Ainsi, en Côte d’Ivoire, on « s’enjaille » à volonté pour s’amuser et faire la fête. Avec des amis étudiants togolais en journalisme, nous nous saluions toujours le matin avec des « On dit quoi ? » ou encore « C’est comment ? » en se donnant la main et claquant les doigts. Il nous est donné même d’entendre un « Bon’ arrivée » les matins, une fois en salle de classe ou dans la cour. En bons francophones africains, on se comprend de toute façon de Dakar à Kinshasa. Alors, bon sommet de la Francophonie à Phnom Penh ! omar.diouf@lesoleil.sn

items.title: Nigeria, Saudi Arabia to begin direct Abuja-Jeddah flights in December, says envoy
items.description: Nigeria and Saudi Arabia are set to strengthen their air connectivity, with Saudi Arabia’s national carrier, Saudia Airlines, scheduled to begin direct flights between Abuja and Jeddah in December. Nigerian Ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Dr Yakubu Gambo, disclosed this in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria on Sunday. Gambo said the service would subsequently extend to Lagos and Port Harcourt. He said Kano would retain its existing direct flight arrangement, while additional routes were expected to be operational before the end of the first quarter of 2027. “By December, we will start having Saudi air flights directly from Abuja. And it will scale up to Lagos, Port Harcourt and Kano,” he said. Gambo said the arrangement followed adjustments and engagements with Saudi aviation authorities, who expressed willingness to support direct air connectivity between both countries. He said Saudi Arabia had also indicated readiness to provide technical and financial support for Nigeria to operate flights through its national carrier. According to him, the arrangement will enable Nigerian pilgrims travelling for Hajj and Umrah to fly directly between both countries without transiting through other territories. “They wouldn’t want pilgrims coming for Umrah or Hajj to fly through other territories that may not be safe,” he said. The ambassador said President Bola Tinubu had been briefed on the proposal and welcomed the initiative. He confirmed that direct flights would also be available for Nigerian pilgrims during the 2027 Hajj exercise. The post Nigeria, Saudi Arabia to begin direct Abuja-Jeddah flights in December, says envoy appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Tunisie | Des industriels du textile dénoncent une concurrence déloyale
items.description: Haithem Bouajila, président de la Fédération tunisienne du textile et de l’habillement (FTTH), a mis en garde contre certaines pratiques liées à l’importation de matières et de produits destinés au marché local et qui consistent à déclarer, auprès des autorités compétentes, une valeur financière inférieure aux prix réels pratiqués sur les marchés internationaux, dans le but d’éviter le paiement des obligations fiscales. Dans une déclaration accordée à Mosaïque FM , Haithem Bouajila a précisé que le problème ne réside pas dans les opérations d’importation en elles-mêmes, mais dans l’écart entre la valeur réelle des marchandises importées et les valeurs déclarées. Pour certains produits, les valeurs déclarées ne représentent qu’un quart, voire un cinquième, de leur valeur effective, a-t-il insisté. Et d’expliquer que les entreprises totalement exportatrices dépendent essentiellement de l’importation de matières premières, transformées ensuite en Tunisie avant d’être réexportées sous forme de produits finis à haute valeur ajoutée. À l’inverse, les entreprises qui produisent pour le marché local sont confrontées à la concurrence d’importations dont les valeurs déclarées ne reflètent pas les prix réels. M. Bouajila a insisté sur le fait que la FTTH ne s’oppose ni à l’importation ni aux échanges commerciaux, mais appelle à garantir la déclaration de la valeur réelle des produits importés et à appliquer les règles fiscales et commerciales à tous les opérateurs économiques, sans exception. Il a estimé que ces pratiques ne portent pas seulement préjudice aux ressources de l’État — issues des impôts et des droits de douane — mais nuisent également à la compétitivité des entreprises industrielles tunisiennes. Celles-ci, qui ont investi dans des équipements et des technologies, supporté les coûts de production et créé des emplois, se retrouvent aujourd’hui confrontées à une concurrence ne reposant pas sur des conditions commerciales équitables. Il est à rappeler, dans ce contexte, que les entreprises totalement exportatrices représentent de 83 % à 85 % du total des entreprises du secteur textile habillement en Tunisie (soit entre 1 300 à 1 550 entreprises selon les recensements de l’industrie manufacturière employant 10 personnes ou plus). Bon nombre d’entre elles fonctionnent en partenariat ou avec des capitaux étrangers (notamment européens). I. B. items.title: AGN Chair demands predictable finance as $7.6 million Urban Resilience Facility launches at COP31
items.description: The African Group of Negotiators on Climate Change (AGN) has positioned urban adaptation at the center of the global climate agenda, calling for direct, predictable finance to protect the continent’s most vulnerable city dwellers. Speaking at a high-level special event, AGN Chair, Nana Dr. Antwi-Boasiako Amoah formally welcomed the launch of the Building Climate Resilience with Africa’s Urban Poor (BCRUP) Regional Readiness Project, supported by an initial $7.6 million readiness facility from the Green Climate Fund (GCF). The project marks a vital operational link between high-level diplomatic commitments and grassroots urban survival across ten pioneer African nations. “Across Africa, the urgency of climate action is increasingly measured by the safety and resilience of our cities and communities,” declared Dr. Amoah during his keynote address to ministers, international delegates, and municipal leaders. “As Chairperson of the African Group of Negotiators on Climate Change, I see the BCRUP Regional Readiness Project as an important opportunity to strengthen the link between our collective climate commitments within the adaptation work streams particularly, the Global Goal on Adaptation, National Adaptation Plan, and Loss and Damage, as well as the locally led action needed to achieve meaningful adaptation outcomes.” African urban centers face escalating compound hazards. Flooding, extreme heat waves, water stress, and environmental degradation severely threaten economic productivity and community livelihoods. Residents of informal settlements and underserved municipal neighborhoods endure the highest exposure to these shocks while possessing the fewest resources to recover. Dr. Amoah emphasized that international climate negotiations must bridge the divide between policy frameworks negotiated at global summits and the daily reality of vulnerable residents in secondary cities, municipalities, and informal settlements. “Africa’s climate vulnerability is increasingly evident in its cities, municipalities, and smaller towns – and this what BCRUP stand for and why we align with the programme as it offers practical connection between negotiations and implementation at the grassroot,” Dr. Amoah noted. “From the perspective of climate negotiations, the challenge is not only to secure commitments for climate finance but also to ensure that those commitments translate into locally owned and implementable programs.” The $10 billion operational plan and the GCF facility The newly launched $7.6 million GCF readiness facility represents an initial catalytic step within a broader, long-term regional strategy. In December 2023, during COP28 in Expo City Dubai, BCRUP unveiled its comprehensive 10-Year Implementation Plan (2024–2034). That roadmap outlines an estimated $10 billion investment requirement—approximately $500 million per country—to scale climate-resilient solutions across 20 African pilot countries. To date, BCRUP has already conducted climate risk assessments and hotspot mapping in more than 60 vulnerable urban areas. The newly approved GCF readiness funding will build upon these foundations to strengthen national coordination mechanisms, boost local government planning capacity, and prepare investment-ready project pipelines. “The approval of the US$7.6 million Green Climate Fund facility for BCRUP is a welcome milestone,” Dr. Amoah stated. “It offers an opportunity to strengthen national coordination mechanisms, build the capacity of local authorities, improve climate-risk and infrastructure data, develop Green Climate-Resilient Urban Spatial Plans and Community Adaptation Plans, and prepare an investment-grade program proposal.” The project relies on a multi-institutional governance framework. Championed by the Government of Kenya and hosted with the support of the Republic of Türkiye’s COP31 Presidency, the initiative brings together technical and institutional coordination from UN-Habitat and United Cities and Local Governments of Africa (UCLG Africa), alongside national designated authorities, municipal leaders, and civil society organizations. Road to COP32: From commitments to bankable pipelines As COP31 deliberations continue, the AGN Chair stressed that the ultimate test of any readiness facility is its ability to unlock predictable finance at scale and deliver tangible safety improvements for vulnerable urban dwellers. “Urban resilience must be recognised as a central element of Africa’s adaptation and climate finance agenda,” Dr. Amoah urged delegates. “Finance must reach the local level, and investments must be designed to meet the needs of the people most exposed to climate impacts. Africa must move from commitments to bankable projects and from bankable projects to measurable improvements in the resilience of our communities, but all the success depends on provision of the means of implementation – Financing to scale and in a predictable manner.” Looking ahead, Dr. Amoah signaled that African negotiators intend to maintain momentum through the continent’s next major climate milestone. “Come COP32, in Addis Ababa, we look forward to having a greater conversation aimed at scaling the programme in more Countries across African Cities,” Dr. Amoah concluded.

items.title: Gideon Boako questions Mahama’s $10bn ambition over unpaid teachers’ salaries
items.description: Tano North MP Dr Gideon Boako has questioned the credibility of President John Dramani Mahama’s US$10 billion New Economy Programme, citing delays in the payment of salaries and arrears owed to teachers. He made this known in a write-up issued on Sunday, November 15, in which he argued that the government’s inability to resolve outstanding salary issues affecting thousands of teachers raises concerns about its capacity to mobilise and effectively deploy US$10 billion over four years. Dr Boako cited the alleged non-payment of new salaries to 52,541 promoted teachers, despite their successful promotion, as well as concerns over the placement of teachers who passed promotion examinations. He claimed that although 80,000 teachers passed promotion examinations, only 6,000 had been placed on the appropriate salary scale. The MP also cited newly recruited teachers who, according to him, worked for 17 months without receiving salaries, as well as post-retirement faculty members of Kumasi Technical University who allegedly went 12 months without pay. He further referenced industrial action by teacher unions, including GNAT, NAGRAT and PRE-TAG, on September 25, 2026, over concerns about outstanding payments and other conditions of service. Dr Boako blamed what he described as bureaucratic delays involving the Controller and Accountant-General’s Department, the Ghana Education Service and the Finance Ministry for the prolonged payment challenges. He questioned how a government struggling to meet its existing salary obligations could credibly commit US$2 billion annually to its New Economy Programme. “How does a government that cannot pay a teacher’s GH¢3,500 monthly salary credibly promise $10 billion?” he asked. He added that teachers affected by the delays would not easily forget the government’s handling of their concerns. “But teachers marking scripts without pay have long memories. Nurses without allowances have long memories,” he stated. Dr Boako said the government must demonstrate its ability to meet existing financial obligations before making further ambitious investment commitments.

items.title: North Kordofan capital El Obeid: One dead, 45+ injured amid indiscriminate gunfire
items.description: One person has been killed and more than 45 others injured, some seriously, after firearms, including anti-aircraft weapons, were discharged indiscriminately in El Obeid, capital of Sudan’s North Kordofan, amid celebrations over (since disproved) reports that the army had taken control of El Nahud in West Kordofan. One person was killed and more than 45 others sustained varying injuries, some of them serious, after firearms, including anti-aircraft weapons, were fired indiscriminately in the city of El Obeid, the capital of North Kordofan, on Saturday. The incident coincided with residents taking to the streets to celebrate circulating reports that the army had taken control of En Nahud, in West Kordofan. Medical sources confirmed that the injured were taken to hospitals in El Obeid for treatment. According to information obtained by Radio Dabanga, residents had flooded the city’s streets to celebrate reports that En Nahud had been liberated . At the same time, videos circulated showing army forces entering the Khamas area in West Kordofan on Saturday. The footage fuelled optimism and prompted residents to express their joy by firing weapons into the air. However, it later emerged that reports claiming the army had entered El Nahud were false. items.title: Sports équestres: «Monde entier» s’offre la couronne nationale à Ouagadougou
items.description: Le cheval «Monde entier», propriété de Donatien Nikiéma, a remporté le championnat national des sports équestres, disputé, le samedi 14 novembre 2026 à l’hippodrome de Hamdalaye, à Ouagadougou. Organisée par la Fédération burkinabè des sports équestres (FBSE), en partenariat avec la Loterie nationale burkinabè (LONAB), cette compétition a été marquée par six courses et une volonté affichée de promouvoir davantage la filière équine nationale. L’hippodrome de Hamdalaye a vécu au rythme des sabots et de la compétition, le samedi 14 novembre 2026. À l'occasion du championnat national des sports équestres, les chevaux engagés, venus des différentes ligues du Burkina Faso, ont rivalisé de vitesse et d'endurance pour inscrire leurs noms au palmarès de cette édition. La course au titre a finalement souri à «Monde entier». Appartenant à Donatien Nikiéma, le cheval a dominé la sixième et dernière épreuve, disputée sur une distance de 2 800 mètres, pour s'adjuger le sacre national. Cette performance lui vaut le prix du ministère des Sports, de la Jeunesse et de l’Emploi, assorti d’un trophée et d’une enveloppe d’un million de francs CFA. Derrière le vainqueur, «Pache», propriété d’Aziz Zoungrana, s’est hissé à la deuxième place avec une récompense de 500 000 F CFA. «RTB», appartenant à Rachid Nacoulma, complète le trio de tête et empoche 250 000 F CFA. Les quatrième et cinquième concurrents repartent respectivement avec 125 000 et 75 000 F CFA. La cinquième course, dédiée au prix de la LONAB et disputée sur 2 100 mètres, a, quant à elle, consacré «Yennega». Le cheval d’Aziz Sanfo a franchi le premier la ligne d’arrivée, décrochant ainsi le trophée et une prime de 750 000 F CFA. Il devance « Timb Nooma », propriété de Souleymane Tiendrébéogo, qui reçoit 400 000 F CFA, tandis que « Jolie Dam » s'adjuge la troisième place avec 200 000 F CFA. Les quatrième et cinquième concurrents ont respectivement obtenu 100 000 et 50 000 F CFA. La LONAB fidèle au rendez-vous des sports équestres Dieudonné Vebamba, a salué une initiative qui participe à la promotion du cheval et à la vitalité de cette discipline Partenaire de cette compétition, la LONAB entend maintenir son accompagnement en faveur du développement des sports équestres au Burkina Faso. Représentant le directeur général de l'institution, son conseiller technique, Dieudonné Vebamba, a salué une initiative qui participe à la promotion du cheval et à la vitalité de cette discipline. «La LONAB accompagne toujours la Fédération burkinabè des sports équestres pour l’organisation du championnat chaque année. Alors, c’est pour nous, en tout cas, une immense joie et une grande fierté de toujours accompagner ce sport», a-t-il souligné. Il a également adressé ses félicitations à l'ensemble des jockeys qui ont pris part aux différentes épreuves. Du côté de la FBSE, le bilan de cette édition est également jugé satisfaisant. Son président, Rachid Nacoulma, s'est réjoui du bon déroulement des courses, qui se sont achevées sans incident. Il a notamment apprécié le comportement des différents acteurs ainsi que le respect du chronogramme établi avec le partenaire pour les paris. «Les entraîneurs, les propriétaires, les jockeys se sont bien comportés lors de la compétition et nous avons aussi respecté le timing concernant aussi la LONAB pour les paris. Donc nous sommes vraiment satisfaits et nous félicitons l’équipe qui a vraiment travaillé pour que le championnat ait lieu», s’est-il réjoui. Président de la FBSE, Rachid Nacoulma Au-delà de la compétition, le président de la FBSE a particulièrement mis en exergue une initiative de cette édition : l'organisation de paris sur les chevaux locaux directement à l'hippodrome, à l'occasion de la sixième course. Pour lui, cette innovation constitue un levier intéressant pour donner davantage de visibilité aux chevaux élevés au Burkina Faso, tout en contribuant à la dynamisation de la filière équine nationale. Les acteurs de la filière à l'honneur Représentant la ministre des Sports, de la Jeunesse et de l’Emploi, le chargé de mission Bagora Bado a également salué la réussite de ce rendez-vous national. Il a adressé ses félicitations au président de la FBSE et à l'ensemble du comité d'organisation pour les efforts consentis en vue de la tenue de la compétition. «Nous tenons au nom de la camarade ministre des Sports, de la Jeunesse et de l’Emploi à féliciter le président de la Fédération burkinabè des sports équestres et tout le comité d’organisation pour avoir ici cette organisation», a-t-il ajouté. Le représentant la ministre des Sports, de la Jeunesse et de l’Emploi, Bagora Bado Le représentant de la ministre a, par ailleurs, rendu hommage aux différents maillons de la chaîne équestre, notamment les éleveurs, les entraîneurs et les jockeys, dont l'investissement demeure essentiel à la pratique de cette discipline. «Nous savons qu’entretenir un cheval, ce n’est pas aussi simple», a-t-il déclaré, avant de remercier l'ensemble de ces acteurs pour leur engagement et leur contribution à la réussite de l'événement. Au terme de cette édition, le sacre de «Monde entier» vient couronner une journée de compétition riche en performances. Mais au-delà des trophées et des récompenses financières, ce championnat aura surtout permis de remettre en lumière le potentiel des sports équestres burkinabè et les perspectives de valorisation des chevaux locaux, avec l'accompagnement renouvelé des partenaires institutionnels. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Sports équestres: «Monde entier» s’offre la couronne nationale à Ouagadougou est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Consider midterm election if you want to extend presidential term from four to five years — Akyem Muosohene
items.description: Chief of Akyem Muoso Osabarima Dr Owusu Beyeeman says extending the presidential and parliamentary term from four to five years without putting measures to check accountability may be catastrophic to Ghana’s young democracy. Speaking at the 2026 YENSOM FESTIVAL of the Chiefs and people of Akyem Muoso, Osabarima Dr Owusu Beyeeman indicated that one year term of non-performing President could be disastrously long nightmare and detrimental to Ghanaians. He said, “On the other hand, a five year term with two term tenure for a perfectly performing president could be short-lived for Ghanaians. According to Osabarima Dr Owusu Beyeeman, in order to ensure accountability and safeguard Ghana’s development, it is incumbent to introduce a midterm election in Ghana to reduce or increase the powers of the executive if we intend to stick to the constitutional review committee’s proposal for a five year term. ‘ If you have a bad president, one year can be hell, but if you have a good president, five years may not even be enough. We should introduce the midterm elections to enable voters to either reduce or maintain the executive powers depending on the president’s performance. Osabarima Dr Owusu Beyeeman noted. The Muosohene proposed that if the five year term is to be adopted, then the country should hold a midterm election in the middle of the five years. This election will determine the fate of the president as to whether they will continue to control the legislation or it will slip to the opposition party. The election will also determine the mood of the citizens as to how the president is performing. He says this arrangement will ensure that a president does not abuse powers or make decisions that will have dire consequences on the nation. Touching on matters related to the development of Akyem Muoso, Osabarima Dr. Owusu Beyeeman indicated that the Muoso ten years development plan launched in the year 2025 is in motion. He indicated that about 40% of the plan spanning infrastructure development, security, education, sanitation, and reclamation, among others, have been realised. According to Osabarima Dr Owusu Beyeeman, a fully furnished police station has been completed. He said that beyond the completion of the ultramodern police station, several other projects are at various stages of completion. Those under various stages of completion include an ultramodern KG school block, coommunity shops and guest house, a 26-seater public toilet facility with shower bathrooms, a 16-seater public toilet facility with shower bathrooms and a 5,000-seater ultramodern community centre with a large parking lot ‘Nananom, these projects represent more than physical structures. They are part of our commitment to building a community where people can live with dignity, where children can learn in better surroundings and where opportunities can be created for the benefit of all’ Osabarima Dr Owusu He said the construction of the Muoso Palace and the proposed Muoso Senior High School are yet to be commenced under the ten year development plan.

items.title: Silence, ils volent nos voix (par Samba Oumar FALL)
items.description: Votre téléphone sonne. À l’autre bout du fil, la voix de votre petit frère, cassée, essoufflée. Il a eu un accident. La police l’a embarqué. Il lui faut de l’argent, vite, et surtout, vous ne devez en parler à personne. Votre cœur s’emballe avant même que votre raison ne s’éveille. C’est bien lui, vous reconnaissez sa voix, ce petit tremblement quand il a peur. Sauf que ce n’est peut-être pas lui. Voilà où nous en sommes aujourd’hui. Les escrocs avaient volé nos sous, nos codes secrets, nos identités. Ils volent maintenant nos voix. Le clonage vocal n’a plus rien d’une curiosité de film américain. Le 6 novembre, la Commission de protection des données personnelles a prévenu que des cas avaient été signalés au Sénégal et dans la sous-région. Ecobank Côte d’Ivoire avait alerté ses clients dès juillet. Et à Touba, en février, la police a démantelé un réseau d’escroquerie et de chantage qui s’appuyait sur l’intelligence artificielle. Interpol l’écrit noir sur blanc. La fraude dopée à l’intelligence artificielle rapporte désormais 4,5 fois plus que les méthodes d’hier. Quand le crime devient plus rentable, il recrute. Les outils de clonage, eux, se vendent désormais presque comme des téléphones. Selon une étude de NordVPN, le commerce qui leur est consacré sur le web clandestin a été multiplié par 7,4 en deux ans. Chez nous, le terrain est fertile. Dans une enquête sur les arnaques par messagerie, plus de 75 % des victimes sénégalaises avaient perdu de l’argent, et WhatsApp, notre salon commun, était le canal le plus cité. Nous vivons par le téléphone, nous envoyons de l’argent d’un clic, nous nous écrivons des vocaux à toute heure. Pour un voleur, c’est un marché ouvert. Songeons à nos familles que la diaspora relie, un fils à l’étranger, une mère à Dakar, un appel, un transfert. Cette chaîne d’amour à distance, qui fait vivre tant de foyers, est le rêve de l’escroc, car l’éloignement empêche de vérifier d’un simple regard, et que la panique laisse trop peu de temps au doute. Le plus cruel, c’est que le piège ne vise pas notre bêtise. Il vise notre amour. Personne ne se fait voler parce qu’il est naïf, mais parce qu’il aime et qu’il veut protéger. L’escroc le sait et c’est son métier de le savoir. Il fabrique l’urgence, parce qu’un cœur qui bat vite réfléchit mal. Il exige le silence, parce qu’un conseil de famille ruinerait son numéro. Il réclame un transfert immédiat, de ceux qui ne reviennent jamais. Chaque seconde que vous prenez pour réfléchir est une seconde qu’il perd. Et la matière première, c’est nous qui la fournissons. Quelques secondes de voix suffisent, et nous en semons partout, une vidéo de baptême, un direct sur TikTok, une cérémonie filmée, un message vocal de trois minutes envoyé sans y penser. Nous publions pour partager. D’autres collectent pour tromper. Mais faut-il alors se taire, cesser de publier, de rire en public ? Non. Ce serait donner raison aux voleurs, et renoncer à la voix qui console, qui félicite, qui bénit, notre plus vieille manière d’aimer. Il faut seulement admettre une vérité désagréable. Reconnaître une voix ne suffit plus pour reconnaître une personne. Alors on change nos habitudes. On raccroche, on respire, on rappelle au numéro habituel. On convient en famille d’un mot de passe que personne d’autre ne connaît, comme jadis, enfants, nous en inventions un pour entrer dans la cachette des grands. On explique à nos parents, cibles de choix, qu’un proche en détresse qui exige le secret n’est pas un proche, quelle que soit la voix qui le réclame, même la plus tendre, même la plus pressante. Et l’on demande aux banques et aux opérateurs d’arrêter de croire qu’une voix familière vaut une pièce d’identité. Certains y verront de la méfiance, voire un peu de paranoïa. Mais il ne faut y voir que de la tendresse bien armée. Ceux qui ricanent aujourd’hui seront peut-être les premiers à pleurer demain, car l’escroc ne choisit pas ses victimes selon leur instruction, mais selon leur affection. Raccrocher pour rappeler son frère, ce n’est pas le soupçonner. C’est le protéger. Alors, le jour où la voix de votre mère vous suppliera, en larmes, d’envoyer de l’argent sans rien dire à personne, faites le geste le plus difficile du monde. Raccrochez. Si c’est elle, elle rappellera. Une mère en danger rappelle toujours, et elle sera fière que vous ayez eu la tête assez froide pour douter de sa voix . Si c’est un escroc, il ne rappellera pas. Il aura déjà composé le numéro suivant, avec la voix d’une autre mère . Par Samba Oumar FALL
